title: The Fall and the Origin of Sin
lead: The story of the first humans' disobedience in Genesis 3, and the doctrines built on it: original sin in the West, ancestral sin in the Eastern churches, the evil inclination in Judaism. Paul's comparison of Adam and Christ (Romans 5) is the key New Testament text.

sections.b: The Old Testament rarely points back to Genesis 3 by name, but it describes the human heart as bent toward evil (Genesis 6:5; 8:21; Psalm 51:5; Jeremiah 17:9). Jewish writings of the Second Temple period took up the story: "through the devil's envy death entered the world" (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24), and 2 Esdras 7:118 laments Adam's fall. Paul writes that "sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin" (Romans 5:12), and that in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive (1 Corinthians 15:22). Augustine developed original sin and inherited guilt; the Orthodox churches teach inherited mortality and weakness; the rabbis taught that each person has a good and an evil inclination and is free to choose. Revelation ends with the curse removed (Revelation 22:3).
sections.refs: Genesis 3:1–24; Genesis 6:5; Genesis 8:21; Psalm 51:5; Jeremiah 17:9; Romans 5:12–21; 1 Corinthians 15:21–22; Revelation 22:3
